note: ICS 630-01 Annex H (ANNEX H - Macedonian_Personal_Names_FLTS (U).pdf), p. 2 (letter table); held source interscript-private-references/ics-630-01/ANNEX H - Macedonian_Personal_Names_FLTS (U).pdf. Extraction: annex text layer, every value cell cross-checked against the rendered page image. Each printed cell gives both cases (e.g. "А а | A a"); transcribed as two rows per cell (upper -> upper value, lower -> lower value). The dze row’s letter cell prints "S s" — a substitute-glyph rendering of Cyrillic Ѕ ѕ in this annex (verified visually; the Macedonian alphabet has no Latin S between З and И, and the value Dz dz is the standard dze romanization) — the row is transcribed as Ѕ -> Dz / ѕ -> dz and, failing end-to-end, recorded as a finding. The text layer for the same cell stores "Ss"/"Dz dz". Skipped printed rows: ’ (apostrophe sign) — printed value cell "[Not represented]" — instruction cell, no romanization value. | Ѕ/ѕ (dze) — printed value cell "Dz dz" FAILS end-to-end on the Cyrillic key: the map encodes the annex’s substitute glyphs literally (Latin S/s, U+0053/U+0073 -> Dz/dz) while the actual Cyrillic dze letters Ѕ/ѕ (U+0405/U+0455) carry no rule and pass through unchanged ("Ѕ" -> "Ѕ"). Finding, never forced green. Findings (map-vs-source, map untouched): Ѕ/ѕ (U+0405/U+0455): printed row Dz/dz untestable — the map has no rule for the Cyrillic dze letters; it instead maps Latin S/s -> Dz/dz (the annex’s substituted letter cell taken literally), so Cyrillic dze passes through unencoded AND Latin-letter input is silently rewritten to Dz/dz, against the annex’s own convention of spelling Latin-letter names as-is.
